blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Desk | Deliver Exceptional Customer Support
blueprint.metaDescription: Explore Zoho Desk, customer support software for businesses and support teams. Streamline tickets, automate workflows, and improve service with omnichannel support and AI assistance.

sections.backgroundTreatment: light split hero with subtle dashboard-panel depth and soft indigo support glow
sections.designNote: Primary goal: immediate message continuity and product clarity. Narrative mode: direct, efficient, enterprise-friendly. Trust strategy: logos-first later, but hero still leads with a compact support/credibility line. Visual dominance: hero-product, so the right side should show a polished Zoho Desk dashboard mockup with ticket queues, omnichannel chips, and AI suggestion cards. CTA aggression: strong enough to convert warm traffic, but keep the hero focused on continuity from the ad. Recommended hero style: split-left-text-right-image. Headline must answer what it is; subheadline must answer who it is for; CTA should be the single required label: Get started.

Use 3-6 recognisable logos in a clean static flex-wrap grid to establish trust early. Since the provided content does not include clear customer logos, interpret this as a partner/brand trust band with recognisable ecosystem or customer logos if available; otherwise fall back to a concise metric strip. Keep it tight and high-contrast against the hero. This section should feel quieter and more evidence-driven than the opening.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: How Zoho Desk works in under 60 seconds

sections.designNote: Insert a warm-traffic process section here to match expected conversion architecture. Keep it to 3 steps and under 60 seconds: capture, organize, resolve. Use a split panel format with a compact visual preview on one side and numbered steps on the other. This breaks the rhythm after the logo trust bar and prevents the page from becoming feature-grid generic. Keep CTA presence minimal here.

This section should spotlight the click-driving value: omnichannel support, ticket management, AI assistance, and workflow automation. Use a spotlight intro for the first product block, then a compact grid for supporting features. Because there are 5+ features across product blocks, do not use a flat static card grid. The first block should feel visual-first and premium, with a dashboard preview or channel-layer graphic. This is the main functional explanation section, so keep it structured and readable.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: Make smarter support decisions with Zia AI

sections.designNote: Treat the AI section as a second product block with a different energy from the previous one. Use an accordion-with-visual so the copy stays dense but not overwhelming. Highlight AI-powered responses, sentiment analysis, auto-tagging, and conversation intelligence. This section should feel more intelligent and analytical than the earlier omnichannel section, creating contrast in layout and tone.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: Integrate with popular apps and the Zoho ecosystem

sections.designNote: Use tabs with a preview panel for the large integration/customization set. This is the best fit for 5+ items and avoids a flat grid. Group integrations, layouts, blueprints, extensions, and help center capabilities into manageable tabs. The preview panel should show a configurable help desk interface rather than a generic diagram. This section should be dense but orderly, reinforcing control and flexibility.

Keep pricing compressed and simple. Use a centered highlighted card with the plan inclusions clearly listed and a single CTA: Get started. Since price values are absent, emphasize what’s included rather than numeric comparison. This should feel like a calm decision point after the feature-heavy middle, not a hard sell.

With 5 testimonials available, use a carousel-static or controlled grid with strong quote hierarchy. Keep the section visually lighter than product blocks and more human. The goal is credibility through operational outcomes: faster responses, lower ticket volume, better visibility, and improved customer satisfaction. Include names and roles prominently.

Final conversion section should be a floating centered card with strong contrast and minimal distraction. Use the single CTA label Get started, full-width on mobile, in accent color at full opacity. Keep this section task-focused and easy to complete, with a clear closing value statement above the form. Since form fields are not provided, keep it lightweight and flexible.

blueprint.designPersonality: Calm, intelligent, enterprise-friendly, and conversion-focused. The page should feel like a modern support command center: white space, structured cards, indigo action accents, strong partner-logo trust bars, and subtle product intelligence cues. Premium but approachable, with no clutter and no dark premium SaaS styling.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use a clean product-led composition: right-side Zoho Desk dashboard mockup, floating chips for omnichannel channels, AI suggestion cards, ticket status pills, and subtle interface depth. Supporting visuals should use SVG logos in trust bands and PNG UI screens; hero visuals can be high-resolution JPEG or polished composite UI imagery.
blueprint.primaryGoal: Convert warm traffic into product engagement by matching the ad message, proving trust early, and leading the user from simple explanation to CTA.
blueprint.additionalInstructions:
PROOF STRATEGY: The visitor trusts logos most. Make this the dominant trust signal.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-panel banner hero with brand/logo at top, large left-aligned headline, short supporting line, and a compact benefits list using icon-ticks; strong product-first framing rather than split hero.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero at the top, followed by a lead-capture/form block, then stacked feature sections with clear fold-based progression; content moves from promise to proof to functional detail.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primarily flat content blocks with minimal decoration; form area uses a contained card treatment, while feature content appears in simple grid/list structures without heavy visual effects.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary conversion is lead capture via form submission rather than repeated button CTAs; CTA hierarchy is implied through form prominence and task-oriented section headings.
referenceMap.footerMode: Not visible in provided reference; footer pattern cannot be inferred.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the visible reference; logo mark in hero and icon bullets for supporting claims. No dominant imagery, product screenshots, or media panels are present.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Sequential feature-led sections with strong headline, short description, and multi-item feature grids; supports progressive disclosure by grouping capabilities into thematic blocks.
referenceMap.formPattern: Prominent lead form placed directly after hero in a bordered container/card; uses stacked fields with hidden tracking inputs and a clear title, optimized for conversion capture.
referenceMap.animationStyle: No explicit animation pattern is inferable from the provided HTML; structure suggests a static, conversion-oriented layout.
designNotes: Conversion-first structure with immediate form proximity to the hero.

Pattern relies on simple hierarchy and modular sections rather than interactive UI complexity.
Good fit for B2B product landing pages that need fast scanning and lead generation.

designStrategy.reasoning: Zoho Desk is a mature B2B customer support product, so the page should optimize for lead generation with a warm audience already aware of the category. The strongest conversion path is proof-led: show what the product does, then reinforce trust with logos, customer scale, testimonials, and functional feature depth. Because visitors trust logos most, the trust band must be prominent and early. A split hero fits the brand-style reference while keeping the message strong, compact, and conversion-focused. The layout should stay clean and readable with balanced density, moving from promise to proof to product capability to plan inclusions and testimonials, while maintaining a sticky top strip and full-page visibility from the start.
